t: Schema definition standard — Tool Input and Output Schema Registry
title: Schema definition standard — Tool Input and Output Schema Registry
description:
The tool input/output schema registry records, for every tool, exactly what it accepts and what it returns: field names, types, required vs optional, value ranges, and validation rules. Planners use it to wire tools together correctly; validators use it to reject bad calls before they run; and version diffs of schemas catch breaking changes before they break pipelines. It is the contract layer the whole tool ecosystem stands on.

This record documents the schema definition standard approach: Define schemas in a shared IDL so every tool's contract looks the same to planners.

Teaching ladder rank 1 (foundations): this record explains the core idea in plain terms — what inputs the tool takes, what outputs it produces, and when it is the right choice for an archive task.

Every record in this database is the full fully-formed file with all data — never a stub or description alone. This database holds 15 of the 1,000,000 target — the march to a million is in progress.
provenance: Public-harvest: documents established, real-world methods for tool input and output schema registry; fact-checked public knowledge.
